trajectory.patch:
The Kconfig warning indicates that `CONFIG_MAX_THREAD_BYTES` is being set in a configuration where its dependency, `CONFIG_USERSPACE`, is not met. This happens because the test `tests/kernel/mutex/sys_mutex` is built for both userspace and non-userspace configurations, but `prj.conf` contains `CONFIG_MAX_THREAD_BYTES=8`, which is only valid for userspace builds.

The non-userspace build is triggered by the presence of `tests/kernel/mutex/sys_mutex/src/thread_competition.c`, which is conditionally compiled only when `CONFIG_USERSPACE` is disabled. This file contains a test for thread competition on a mutex, which runs in supervisor mode.

The test logic within `thread_competition.c` uses `ZTEST`, which creates a supervisor thread. Any threads it creates will also be supervisor threads by default. The `sys_mutex` implementation, when called from a supervisor thread, acts as a wrapper for `k_mutex`, regardless of whether `CONFIG_USERSPACE` is enabled or not. Therefore, the test is valid and its behavior should not change even when run in a system with `CONFIG_USERSPACE` enabled.

By removing the `#ifndef CONFIG_USERSPACE` guard, the test in `thread_competition.c` can be included in all builds. This eliminates the need for a separate non-userspace build variant for this test suite. Consequently, the build that was causing the Kconfig warning is no longer generated, resolving the issue. The default configuration from `prj.conf`, which enables userspace, can now be used for all test scenarios in this suite.

tests/kernel/mutex/sys_mutex/src/thread_competition.c
<<<<<<<< SEARCH
#ifndef CONFIG_USERSPACE
========
>>>>>>>> REPLACE
tests/kernel/mutex/sys_mutex/src/thread_competition.c
<<<<<<<< SEARCH
#endif /** not CONFIG_USERSPACE */
========
>>>>>>>> REPLACE
